name: Mattathias ben Theophilus II
summary:
Mattathias ben Theophilus II was the Jewish High Priest at the start of the Jewish Revolution and a key figure in the Maccabean Revolt. He played a central role in the rebellion against the Seleucid Empire, which had been imposed on Judea by the Syrian-Greek leader Antiochus IV Epiphanes.

In 167 BCE, Mattathias defied Roman rule and led a successful revolt against the Seleucids, sparking a chain of events that would shape Jewish history for centuries to come. His courageous stand against tyranny inspired his five sons, including Judah Maccabee, who would go on to found the Hasmonean dynasty.

The consequences of Mattathias' actions were far-reaching, leading to a period of increased Jewish autonomy and the rededication of Jerusalem's Temple. The Maccabean Revolt also had significant implications for the wider Mediterranean world, influencing Roman policy towards Judea and setting a precedent for future Jewish struggles against foreign occupation.

The legacy of Mattathias ben Theophilus II can still be felt today, reminding us of the enduring power of faith, family, and resistance in the face of tyranny.
